description:
Issue summary:
Customer NovaSearch reported a sudden spike in 5xx (503) responses and p99 inference latency starting 2026-03-11 21:10 UTC. Traffic was diverted to a quantized GPU fallback variant that appears to be in a warmup/initializing state on a single rack, causing serial cold-starts and temporary capacity exhaustion.

Impact:
- Intermittent 503s and p99 latency > 12s for search reranking calls between 21:10–21:48 UTC.
- Around 18% of requests for particular routes returned 503 during the peak window.
- Customer-facing application experienced degraded search relevance and increased error rates across user sessions.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted dedicated pool (NovaSearch reserved cluster), prod-us-east-1, model routing policy uses auto-fallback: primary -> quantized-gpu-fallback -> cpu-fallback.
- Autoscaler set: min_replicas=2, max_replicas=16, scale_window=30s.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Send high-concurrency reranking traffic (500 qps sustained) to route /v1/engines/rerank-nova/complete.
2) Observe 503s and rising p99 after primary model saturates.
3) Notice fallback routing to quantized-gpu variant that reports "initializing" for several seconds before reporting "active".

Observed behavior:
- Router diverted bursts of traffic to the quantized GPU variant even when the variant reported replica_count_active=0 and replica_count_initializing>0.
- The fallback variant entered a warmup queue causing serial warmups on a single rack; each new replica initialization introduced a ~6–10s coldstart window and transient 503s as worker rlimits and model load completed.
- Autoscaler did not pre-warm replicas quickly enough; routing continued to send traffic to the fallback instead of temporarily redirecting back to primary or CPU variant.

Expected behavior:
- Fallback routing should prefer variants with replica_count_active>0 and sufficient in-flight capacity and should throttle/divert burst traffic to CPU fallback or queue requests rather than pushing to initializing replicas that will 503.

Logs/observations:
- Router trace: router-id=rt-13b7, decision_time=21:11:03.124Z, selected_variant=quantized-gpu-v2, variant_state=initializing, active_replicas=0, initializing_replicas=1.
- Serving runtime (worker) logs show model load + CUDA memory reservation spikes and repeated worker process restarts during the window.
- Cloud metrics: GPU memory pressure on rack-r3 spiked to 98% when the quantized variant started loading.
- Error samples (gateway): 503: upstream worker-init-failed: model_load_timeout after 9.8s.

Impact to customer SLA and billing:
- Errors occurred for dedicated customer traffic; billing impact is likely due to retried requests. Customer flagged as high priority since reranking errors affect production search.
steps_to_reproduce: Generate sustained high qps (500 qps) to rerank route in prod-us-east-1
Monitor router decisions and count of replica states for fallback variants
Observe that router sends traffic to initializing quantized replicas causing worker model-load timeouts
investigation_notes: 21:15 UTC: SG contact confirmed spike coincides with a regional traffic surge and a simultaneous canary rollout for quantized variant
Router policy TTL was observed to be 0s during burst — router re-evaluated per-request and selected fallback aggressively
Autoscaler logs show scale-up events but replicas entered 'initializing' state sequentially due to constrained rack disk I/O and KV cache priming time
Hypothesis A: routing policy lacks active-replica gating and will route to 'initializing' variants under burst when primary capacity exhausted
Hypothesis B: quantized model artifacts on rack had stale/corrupted shard leading to extended model_load times and occasional worker restarts
actions_taken: Added temporary router rule to prefer cpu-fallback for NovaSearch rerank route at 21:30 UTC to stop further 503s
SRE increased autoscaler burst_limit for the dedicated pool to allow faster provisioning at 21:34 UTC
Pulled worker logs and flagged failing model artifact; a checksum mismatch was observed for one shard and removed at 21:40 UTC
Opened GH PR to add active_replica gating to router decision logic: PR #2381
current_findings: Primary model saturated and fallback decision logic selected initializing quantized replicas due to lower cost score — but routing didn't check active_replica_count > 0
One rack (rack-r3) had high disk latency causing sequential model load delays — this serialized replica readiness and amplified coldstart windows
After switching to cpu-fallback and removing bad shard, error rate dropped to baseline by 21:48 UTC
workaround: Applied temporary router override to prefer cpu-fallback for affected route and increased autoscaler burst; this mitigated error burst. Customer notified and asked to keep override until patch is deployed.
resolution: In progress - short term workaround applied. Engineering intends to merge PR #2381 (router: require active_replicas > 0 or recent_ready_time < 10s gating) and a placement fix to avoid serial warmups on single rack. Post-deploy will include canary and traffic shaping to prevent future coldstart cascades.
postmortem_followup_items: Router: enforce active-replica gating and add a temporary penalty for 'initializing' variants during bursts
Autoscaler: add parallel initialization tuning to avoid rack-saturation serial loads
Artifact pipeline: add shard checksum verification and faster fallback to alternative artifact store if corrupted
Console: surface variant readiness and per-variant warmup latency in rerouting decisions

2026-03-12 22:18 UTC — SRE (Maya Ortiz): 'Found disk io spikes on rack-r3 and repeated model_load_timeout in worker logs. Increasing autoscaler burst helps but we need router changes.'
2026-03-12 22:35 UTC — Engineer (Ava Chen): 'Opened PR #2381 to add gating; will coordinate canary after QA. Applying temporary router override now.'
2026-03-12 22:50 UTC — Customer (NovaSearch - Eng lead, Priyanka Rao): 'We see error rate drop — thanks. Please keep us posted on permanent fix and any risk to ongoing workloads.'
2026-03-14 09:12 UTC — Engineering Manager (Diego Fernández): 'Targeting fast-track merge and hotfix deploy on 2026-03-15; will update timeline after canary metrics.'
notes_for_qa: Verify router decision now requires variant.active_replicas > 0 for fallback unless forced by admin. Simulate burst traffic with a single initializing replica and ensure traffic is diverted to cpu-fallback. Confirm no increased p99 during canary.
customer_communication: 2026-03-12 23:05 UTC: Notified customer of temporary routing override and mitigation steps. Will provide follow-up post hotfix deploy. Customer asked for timeline and confirmation that retries will be gated to avoid duplicate charges.
